fr.elements: Main Residence; Front Driveway; Vehicle Parking Area; Walkway; Open Green Space; Perimeter Fencing; Street Frontage
fr.considerations: Single Access Point; Open Terrain; Fenced Sections
fr.recommendations:
• Mark the driveway entrance with reflective address numbers visible from both directions on the street.
• Keep the driveway clear of parked vehicles to allow emergency vehicles to reach the residence.
• Install a reflective address marker at the street to help responders locate the property quickly at night or in low visibility.
• Keep the perimeter fence gates unlocked or use a combination lock with the code posted for emergency responders.
• Mark any locked gate with the access code or key location in a format visible to arriving responders.
• Keep the walkway between the street and front entry clear of obstructions at all times.
• Maintain the open green space adjacent to the driveway free of equipment, vehicles, or stored materials that would block emergency vehicle staging.

wildfire.conditions: Scattered Shrubs; Tree Cluster; Grass Cover; Open Terrain; Adequate Vegetation Separation; Scattered Trees; Single Access Route; Limited Rear Access; Open Green Space; Woody Debris
wildfire.recommendations:
• Remove woody debris piles visible near structures before fire season.
• Thin the tree cluster closest to the structure to increase open space between tree canopy and the building.
• Cut grass around structures and outbuildings short, particularly during dry months.
• Trim low-hanging branches on scattered trees near the house to reduce the path fire can travel from the ground upward.
• Clear shrubs growing directly adjacent to or touching any structure.
• Keep the single access route free of overhanging branches and encroaching vegetation so vehicles can pass through without obstruction.
• Remove dead or dry woody material that has collected along the rear of the property where access is limited.
• Thin shrubs in the rear yard area to allow better movement around the back of the structure.
• Keep the open green space areas mowed and free of accumulated dead grass or plant debris.
• Separate any remaining shrub groupings near structures so fire cannot move continuously from one shrub to the next toward the building.
